solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support contract in Australia is something to count on

indicators.note: in says the shortened support word sits inside the abbreviation for Australia
to contract is to shrink, so the support word loses its last letter

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A backing deal signed in Australia sounds like a dependable thing to rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to count on' reads as 'reliable'; literally it is a counting frame. BACK shortened by 'contract' gives BAC, placed 'in' AUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame is used literally for counting, so it is a thing one counts on.

clue.text: Set trailer everyone's jumping on?

parts.note: a band is a group or set
a wagon is a cart or trailer pulled behind

explanation.surface: A trailer that has been prepared for a crowd to climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'jump on the bandwagon' is to join a popular trend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of joining a popular cause is jumping on it, so it is what everyone leaps onto.

clue.text: About to manage church crisis

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: Getting ready to deal with a crisis in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a decisive critical moment, as in 'when it comes to the crunch', so it fits a crisis.

clue.text: Sow centre ground with maize

indicators.note: ground means crushed or broken up, so the letters of sow centre are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planting the middle field with corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a field; it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize kernels eaten as a vegetable go by this name; the crop is the same plant.

clue.text: Rookie is initially trying to be an artist like Picasso

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as in a cub reporter

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word trying

explanation.surface: A beginner is attempting to paint in the manner of Picasso.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, so a painter of that movement is an artist of his kind.

clue.text: Dad's after a pot of tea

indicators.note: after says the father word comes behind the pot word

parts.note: a pot is a trophy, a cup
pa is dad, with 's as is

explanation.surface: Father wants a pot of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is sporting slang for a trophy CUP, not a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial word for a cup of tea, the everyday brew.

clue.text: Kitchen container used as money box?

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a bin is a box or receptacle

explanation.surface: A kitchen tin being used as a piggy bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf is kept in a lidded box on the kitchen counter, a household container.

clue.text: Kind of Muslim to accept verse of Hindu god

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the verse letter goes inside

parts.note: Shia is one of the main branches of Islam

explanation.surface: A Muslim of one branch accepting a verse about a Hindu deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The destroyer deity of the Hindu trinity is known by this name, alongside Brahma and Vishnu.

clue.text: False tooth turned out fine at last

indicators.note: out signals the letters of turned are put out of order
at last picks the final letter of the word fine

explanation.surface: A false tooth came out well in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like a phrase meaning 'proved'; 'out' is the anagram signal on TURNED, giving DENTUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental plate of artificial teeth is called by this name; one false tooth is a stretch but fair.

clue.text: Specialised board for consumers?

parts.note: the surface suggests a consumer watchdog panel, but the board is furniture and the consumers are diners eating at it

explanation.surface: A dedicated committee set up to protect shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is an old word for a table and 'consumers' are those eating at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The piece of furniture people eat meals at is a board used by those consuming food.

clue.text: Prime minister of empire- building Queen?

indicators.note: building suggests the letters of empire are reconstructed into a new arrangement

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A head of government who builds an empire for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like part of 'empire-building' but is the anagram signal; the Queen here is R, Regina, not ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a government is commonly called by this title, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rampant stag encompassing Art Deco style is painted again

indicators.note: encompassing says one group of letters surrounds the other
rampant means rearing wild, so the stag word's letters are thrown about

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: style here means to fashion afresh, so the letters of Art Deco are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heraldic rearing stag surrounded by Art Deco styling, freshly painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' is heraldic, a beast rearing up, but signals an anagram of the stag word, REED; 'style' rearranges the period name to DECORAT, which REED wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate a room is to repaint or refurnish it, so painted again fits.

clue.text: Old Bill's home is modern with a country garden

parts.note: modern means new
Scotland is a country of the UK
in American usage a yard is a garden

explanation.surface: The police station is a modern building with a rural garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police; this is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, the force nicknamed the Old Bill, is so named.

clue.text: Goes on horses

definitions.meaning: to keep complaining at someone, to harp on
old or worn-out horses, also any horse informally

explanation.surface: Goes on horses: someone rides out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: one who keeps complaining, and plural slang for horses.

clue.text: Judgmental about musical trio not suitable for all

indicators.note: about signals the letters of musical trio are turned around and rearranged
not says the letters of the symbol for suitable for all are left out of the mix

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A disapproving review of a three-piece show deemed unfit for family audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: rearrange MUSICAL TRIO, minus the U that 'not suitable for all' removes. U is the British film rating for universal audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone preachy and quick to pass moral judgment on others is described this way.

clue.text: Donkey's working cane crush to loose juice perhaps?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, with 's as is
on means working, as a machine that is on

indicators.note: crush means to squash out of shape, so the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey toils at a cane press to release sugar juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose juice' is an example: the words share a vowel sound without rhyming.
explanation.definitionFit: The repetition of a vowel sound in nearby words, as in the pair given, is the poetic device meant.

clue.text: Deceiver of King's put in strict order by Queen

indicators.note: put in says the king letter is placed inside the rearranged word
order means arrange, so the letters of strict are shuffled

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A royal cheat is ordered by the Queen to follow rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in strict order' reads as 'precisely' but 'order' is the anagram signal, giving TRICST, and 'put in' splits it for the K.
explanation.definitionFit: A con artist or swindler is someone who deceives, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Policeman retains criminal file, noting contents removed: act of corruption

indicators.note: retains means holds onto, so the detective letters surround the rest

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters of file are disordered
contents removed means only the outer letters of noting remain

explanation.surface: A detective keeps a crime record, leaving out the details: a corrupt act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges FILE into EFIL, held by DI; NG is NOTING emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluting or desecrating something is the act of making it impure, a kind of corruption.

clue.text: Sympathy for sore head

parts.note: a sore spot is tender
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Seeking sympathy for a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a body part here but a geographic headland, a NESS as in Loch Ness or Inverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle compassion or warmth of feeling toward another is a near synonym of sympathy.

clue.text: Sample from Fendi or other couturier

indicators.note: Sample from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Try a garment from Fendi or some other fashion house.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior founded a famous Paris fashion house, so the name is another couturier besides Fendi.

clue.text: No good getting in back-up for park keeper

indicators.note: getting in says the two short letters enter the turned word
up in a down clue says the back word is read upward, in reverse

parts.note: rear means back

explanation.surface: A useless backup wanted for the park warden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REAR into RAER, which takes N and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden who looks after a national park or forest is a ranger.

clue.text: China's caught in appalling scam with sporting equipment

indicators.note: caught in says one piece is trapped inside another

parts.note: appalling means bad
a racket is a fraudulent scheme
Minton is a famous English porcelain maker, so its china

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain gets involved in a dreadful swindle involving sports gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but porcelain: MINTON, an English pottery firm, goes 'caught in' BAD RACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The strung bat used to hit a shuttlecock is a piece of sports kit.

clue.text: Pronounce drink to be a powerful spirit

indicators.note: pronounce means say aloud, so the drink word is heard

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Declaring alcohol to be a strong spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests liquor but means a genie.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabian folklore this is a supernatural being, a genie of great power.

clue.text: Plagiarism of article by newspaper

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Copying a piece written for the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarism is stealing someone else's words, a form of stealing.

clue.text: East Germany's providing rocks for building

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
providing means if, as in a condition
ice is slang for diamonds, also called rocks

explanation.surface: East Germany supplying stones for construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' and ICE are both slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A large imposing structure is an edifice, so it is a building.

clue.text: Denied access in revolutionary study

indicators.note: in places the entrance word inside the turned study
revolutionary suggests a turning over, so the study word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study room
a gate gives access

explanation.surface: Someone was refused entry to a radical's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DEN into NED, which holds GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or nullify, so negated works as a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Peer in utter darkness

indicators.note: utter means speak aloud, so the darkness word is heard

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Staring into total darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like the adjective 'complete'; it is the verb 'say'. 'Peer' looks like 'look' but is a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled man ranks with the nobility; strictly a knight is not a peer, but loosely it is a noble rank.

clue.text: Fears taking top off to reveal boobs!

indicators.note: taking top off removes the first letter from the word for fears

parts.note: terrors are fears

explanation.surface: A cheeky saucy-postcard picture of anxieties about undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' is the noun for blunders, not the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs are mistakes or blunders, a British informal synonym.
